claims.text:
stage computation: Approximate f(x)=x² on[0,1] using n equal linear pieces, n∈{1,2,4}. Construct g_n(x)=x/n + sum over k=1..n−1 of (2/n)ReLU(x−k/n). This is the chord interpolant at knots k/n. At segment midpoints maximum absolute error is1/(4n²): .25,.0625,.015625. Compute interpolation values and midpoint error, not a decorative fit.

**Countercase / boundary:** Weights are supplied constructively, not learned. This finite x² example does not prove a universal theorem or that optimization finds a solution. Outside the bounded interval, n4 at x=2 gives2.75 versus4; approximation on[0,1] gives no extrapolation promise.

**Prediction / transfer recall:** Predict whether adding knots reduces this bounded interpolation error; recall n8 bound1/256 under the same construction and distinguish existence from training.

**Intervention / reachable witness:** Add pieces1→2→4 changes ReLU units, chord plot and maximum-error marker; Extrapolate exposes x2 error while retaining bounded error. Display the active coefficients/knots without showing the computed maximum before commitment.
